title: Avatar definition
description: The definition file inside a .morda archive. Targets are written once, under a name, in frames. An expression references those names, so nothing is drawn from a target written inside an expression. A string is read as a name, unless it starts with a marker prefix such as file:, which says what kind of value it is. Names cannot contain a colon, so a marker can never be mistaken for a name. A string with a colon is read as a marker, and a prefix the format does not know is reported as an error. Every file referenced must be present under the name it gives, and a reference to a name the definition does not declare is reported as an error. An expression that shows one frame is written as the name alone; that is the short form of a frame_order with one entry.

name.description: The skin name, the same string a config value or a roster pool entry uses. This is the value used for naming; the directory name and the archive file name are not used.

type.description: Which type of archive this is. It decides how the rest is read, so the reader never guesses from the file list.

frame.description: Frame size in pixels, used only for a sheet.

grid.description: Rows and columns of the sheet. Columns are declared as well as rows, because an expression that can show more than one frame needs its second cell. Used only for a sheet.

frames.description: The targets, each written once under a name. Names are unique inside one definition, so a name is enough to find a target.

sheet.description: The image the cells are cut from. Written as a target, so it is the object form naming a file, or the marker short form of the same thing. Required when type is sheet, because a grid describes an image that is never named without it. Not allowed when type is image, where each expression names its own file.

expressions.description: Each expression name maps to what it walks. An entry here is a reference, not a target.

fallback.description: The frame used for an expression the definition does not name. Without it an unknown expression draws nothing.

object-fit.description: How a frame is placed inside the box that draws it. Written here, it is the setting for every frame in the definition; a target can state its own. The size of the box is not part of a definition, because the box belongs to the view that draws it. A default written here is an annotation, so the reader is what applies it.

fit.description: fill stretches a frame to the box and ignores its shape. contain keeps the whole frame inside the box, so an odd shape leaves empty space on one pair of sides. cover fills the box, so nothing is left empty and what does not fit is cut. none draws at the size the frame reports, which can reach outside the box. scale-down never makes a frame larger, so it is none when the frame is already smaller than the box and contain otherwise. What is shown when a frame is larger than the box is decided by its centre, since there is no position field for a target. Every value is read as nearest-neighbour, so pixels do not blur.

marker.description: A string with a colon, read as a marker: the prefix says the kind, the rest is the value. The prefix is not part of the file name it points at. A marker is only a short form of the object form, so it cannot say anything an object cannot say. A value that needs more than one part, such as a cell, keeps its object form.

row.description: Row in the declared grid. A reader reports a mismatch between the declared grid and the size reported by the PNG header as one error, rather than guessing a grid.

object-fit.description: The setting this target uses instead of the one written for the definition. It needs the object form, because a marker cannot carry a second part.

cell.description: A target named by the kind, so a target says what it is. Same shape as a target naming a file.

file.description: Name of a file in the archive. It may name a file in a subfolder, because an entry path is a name rather than a directory the reader walks, but it is not an absolute path and it has no .. segment, so a definition cannot reach outside the skin folder or the archive.

object-fit.description: The setting this target uses instead of the one written for the definition. A file is placed by the size its own header reports, since an image definition states no size.

oneOf.description: One frame, written as the name alone. Short form of a frame_order holding that one entry.

frame_order.description: The names this expression shows, in order. Named so it cannot be mistaken for the frames map at the top level. A list carries values only, so it cannot hold a time between frames.

interval_ms.description: Whole milliseconds between frames when this expression shows more than one. Written as it is meant to be read, not computed from a rate, because a rate that does not divide 1000 evenly has no exact interval.

loop.description: Optional, default true. After the last entry of frame_order, true goes back to the first entry and shows them again; false stops at the last entry. The default is an annotation, not something a schema validator enforces, so the reader applies it when the field is absent.

oneOf.description: There is no default interval to inherit. An expression that lists more than one name in frame_order has to state its own interval, and one that lists more than one name without stating it is reported as an error. An expression with a single name has no time between frames, so it states none.

allOf.description: A definition that declares no fallback has to declare an entry for neutral, so there is always something it can show for a name it does not cover.
